entries.locator: Full article pp5616-5622; Table I, p5618 selected value/error paragraph, Tables IV-V and Appendix
entries.inspection: Full user-supplied eight-page PDF including publisher cover; relevant scans visually checked
findings: Full-text selected D0=1177+/-11 kJ/mol on p5618; abstract reports1177+/-18. Table I separately gives1177+/-18 and1177+/-12 from reactions2 and3. Hf298=-174+/-14 is unchanged. Preserve all locators instead of silently replacing one uncertainty.

Selected heats at0K for VO+Eu=EuO+V, VO2+V=2VO, VO2+Eu=EuO+VO are158.5+/-6,-74+/-6,84.5+/-6 kJ/mol. With D0(EuO)=467+/-6, both routes giveD0(VO2)=1177 viaD0(VO)=625.5. Reaction temperature ranges are1913-2178,1913-2186,1913-2282K.

The authors define selected reaction and ancillary errors as estimated standard deviations, assuming normal distributed effects, and state reliability within three times the quoted errors. These are not a common confidence convention for all literature sources.

The inferred VO2 energies share VO and EuO references. At fixed reaction heats both respond by2 kJ/mol to a1 kJ/mol change inD0(EuO); separate reaction routes do not justify statistically independent final energies. Full covariance is not supplied.

Appendix/Table V use ground weight2, matrix-derived frequencies983/538/1034cm^-1,95degree angle and estimated0.163nm bonds. V/VO functions remain JANAF-based. The538cm^-1 bend conflicts with later resolved291(2)cm^-1; no excited electronic states included.

Table IV thermal functions and source-specific uncertainties are now accessible. Reconstructing selected-energy algebra and tabulated enthalpy increments does not redo the raw mass-spectrometric analysis or establish a modern replacement.

entries.locator: Energy discussion before table912; molecular constants discussion
entries.role: Expert reevaluation by E.L. Osina and L.N. Gorokhov
entries.inspection: Full online evaluation; publication/revision date not securely established
findings: Reevaluates isomolecular Balducci1983 equilibria VO2+V=2VO and VO2+Eu=EuO+VO; favours pressure ratios over absolute pressures; D0=1166+-12 kJ/mol, Hf298=-160.259+-12.3 kJ/mol.
No new independent measurement relative to Balducci1983. Updated auxiliary data and thermal functions matter.

Its description that JANAF omits excited electronic states agrees with the inspected original page. The atomic V++ level analogy and a hypothetical VO2 state in the JANAF uncertainty discussion must not be mistaken for adopted levels.
Its older0.6eV state assignment follows Wu/Wang1998 and predates the2014 cryo-SEVI reassignment.

entries.role: Primary cryogenic anion photoelectron experiment with calculations
findings: Assigned neutral bent X2A1 ground state, A2B1 at0.1845(8)eV and B2A1 at0.8130(5)eV; v1/v2 measured separately in all three states.
EA1.8357(5)eV revises the2.03(1)eV assignment in Wu/Wang1998; electron affinity is not neutral atomization energy.
Cryogenic ion preparation and resolved distinct progressions reduce hot-anion ambiguities; the third band needs configuration interaction.
No v3 measurement, complete high-temperature partition function, state-specific rotational measurement or formation enthalpy supplied.
DFT/CASPT2/RCCSD(T) study proposes alternate assignments involving near-degenerate anion states.
The assignment dispute is retained, not silently treated as agreement.

entries.inspection: Full text rendered by web provider from author-manuscript mirror; author-host download failed
findings: Authors defend the cold-ion assignments using one-electron orbital transitions, Franck-Condon patterns and source-temperature considerations.
Reply is the same experimental lineage as the original paper, not an independent replication. A complete high-temperature state sum is still missing.
